# Engine E2E shard 2 repeats the six-minute timeout

## Context

The current Engine E2E timing table feeds the existing 15-shard allocation. The fresh Dependabot replacement for #22085, #22099, repeats the shard 2 deadline overrun. The current dev run shows the same limit.

## The Problem

[#22099 Engine Tests](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45175330287) hit the six-minute step limit on shard 2 in three attempts. Attempt 3 reported all 84 tests passing before the deadline. On [dev at `6ed80fc200`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45178592636) shard 2 stopped after 85 of 90 cases. The aggregate remains red on those runs.

## The Architectural Reality

The timing table in `buildScripts/util/e2eEngineDurations.json` feeds the existing deterministic selector and assigns tests by observed file costs. The current workload is 325 specs. The workflow still provides 15 full shards and a 360-second test step.

Design authority: [Whitebox E2E timing refresh guidance](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/6ed80fc200b086dab75527bece60bbed298e11e6/learn/guides/testing/WhiteboxE2E.md#L69-L76) and the measured-refresh option in D#21957.

## The Fix

Regenerate the timing table from the five latest effective green full dev matrices and the complete per-file observations from the newest red dev run. The expected maximum on the independent #22099 retry replay falls from 368.6 to 342.7 seconds of test intervals. The newest dev workload replays at 346.7 seconds with one imputed tail. Hosted CI will measure the actual job steps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Exactly all 325 current Engine E2E specs are assigned once across the existing 15 shards.
- [ ] The timing-only change lowers peak test intervals in the independent dependency replay and documents the newest dev replay and its partial tail.
- [ ] The full repair PR passes the six-minute Engine E2E steps and their aggregate.
- [ ] Post-merge, verify the latest dev run and refresh the dependency PR onto the repaired base.

## Out of Scope

Shard count, step duration, test selection, build dependency versions and publishing.
